No residue field of $R$ is orderable, and \[ \sup_{x\in U}\{\cd_2\kappa(x)+\dim\OO_{U,x}\}=1. \]

exact_statement_tex: \label{thm:birational} Let $f:X\to Y$ be a proper birational morphism of integral noetherian schemes of characteristic $p>0$. If $X$ is normal and $Y$ is regular, then $R^1f_*\OO_X=0$. If, in addition, $X$ and $Y$ are proper varieties over an algebraically closed field $k$, then pullback induces an isomorphism of group schemes \[ \Pic^\tau_{Y/k}\xrightarrow{\sim}\Pic^\tau_{X/k}. \]

exact_statement_tex: \label{thm:boundary} If $Y$ is contained in a quasi-projective open subset of $X$, then $Q(X,Y)$ is topologically finitely generated. In particular, $\pi_1(X\setminus\{x\})$ is topologically finitely generated when $x$ is a closed point of codimension at least two. More generally, if a proper connected variety $Z$ need not be normal and a closed subset has codimension at least two on every irreducible component and has one quasi-projective open neighborhood, the fundamental group of its complement is finitely generated. For normal $X$, the same conclusion for $Q(X,Y)$ holds whenever there is a normal projective modification $X'\to X$ such that the wild inertia at each exceptional divisorial component of the inverse image of $Y$ has finite image in $Q(X,Y)$.

exact_statement_tex: \label{lem:wreath} The kernel $A_0$ of $\Sigma$ is the elementary abelian group $\F_2\oplus V$, with $(b,u)$ corresponding to $(u,u;b)$. The section $v\mapsto(v,0;0)$ makes its $V$-action \[ v\cdot(b,u)=(b,u+bv). \] The map of regular modules \[ \phi:\F_2[V]\longrightarrow A_0,\qquad e_g\longmapsto(1,g) \] is surjective and $V$-equivariant. It induces a surjection $\F_2[V]\rtimes V\twoheadrightarrow G$ over $V$. Moreover, \[ \Ver_{G,H}(x,y;\epsilon)=(x+y,x+y). \]
